The regular-part conclusions match the paper's proof l.2377-2381 and l.2400-2403 and are at least as strong: D injective; rho faithful, discrete and torsion-free; the Gamma-invariant null planes Pi_w; D(Reg M~) = Omega+ = bigcap I+(Pi_w) as an EQUALITY (DEC-28 via Cor 2.18 absolute maximality); a free, properly discontinuous action; Reg M ≃ₜ B as a local isometry, where B is a GH presentation of rho(Gamma)\Omega+ (covering, onto, fibres = orbits). The hypotheses were checked against their definitions. E0CauchyCompact is a compact acausal Cauchy surface (B21's Cauchy-compact, DEC-28). IsE0CauchyMaximal is shown equivalent to Dev.IsETTMaximal by isE0CauchyMaximal_iff_isETTMaximal (DEC-77 (c)). hsing is (chartedSing e0SingY M 0).Nonempty, i.e. s ≥ 1 (DEC-76). None of these is trivial, circular, or carries the conclusion. The only deviations from the ruled hypothesis set are disclosed. (i) Not-metabelian is used in place of DEC-76's non-abelian; see issue 3. (ii) hLine is carried; see issue 4. (iii) SecondCountableTopology M is carried, which is implicit in 'manifold' and matches AbsMax. The tagged sorry asserts ¬ range D ⊆ Omega-(Lambda) under GH + Cauchy-compact + Cauchy-maximal + a BTZ point + not metabelian. This is D-11 (d)'s argument: a BTZ point has a nontrivial stabiliser, so it is not in Omega, and in the past case it would lie in J-(D y~) ⊆ Omega-. The auditor finds it true and adequately hypothesised. The obstruction is genuine: it needs D extended across sing0(M), and the scaffold has no bridge from ChartedSpace E0Y to SingularGXStructure/BTZTildeData. The causal-only alternative the auditor tried fails for the reason the SORRY text gives: a past timelike curve of bounded length in Minkowski need not converge. The dispatch suggests consuming Causal.Flat.equality_of_absMax directly. The file instead consumes range_eq_omegaS_of_absMax with P = True and replays equality_of_absMax's proof to keep the descended map. This was checked and is sound.

issues.problem: DEC-76 is a binding AUTHOR ruling: 'π₁(Σ∖sing) non-abelian'. The file assumes the stronger 'π₁(Reg M) not metabelian'. This is disclosed, and the algebraic counterexample shows why the stronger form is used. However, under DEC-76's own hypothesis the theorem is still true geometrically: π₁ of a punctured surface is free, and a non-abelian free group is not metabelian. So the deviation is a reading the author has not ruled on, and the REPORT raises no question to settle it.
